/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 24 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2743 (18)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4285 (87)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2024 (-40)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1694 (-8)
Baltic Handysize Index: 905 (-1)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the week with further gains, as the BCI 182 5TC advanced $788 to $38,860. Positive sentiment in the Pacific and continued strength from the South Atlantic outweighed softer conditions in the North Atlantic, allowing the market to finish the week on a constructive note. The Pacific remained firm despite relatively limited fresh enquiry. Three major C5 miners were active during the day, providing underlying support to the market. Reports emerged early of a miner fixing at $12.20 overnight, setting a positive tone. As trading progressed, bids continued to strengthen, with a Newcastlemax reportedly fixed at $12.75, while operators were said to be bidding in the upper $12s for standard Capes. The stronger sentiment was reflected in the C5 index, which rose 0.740 to $12.855. Conditions from South Brazil and West Africa to China also continued to improve. Brokers reported bids in the high $34s, with owners maintaining offers around $36, highlighting the widening gap but firmer offers. This supported the C3 index, which gained 0.545 to $34.680. In contrast, the North Atlantic remained subdued, with limited cargo enquiry and a marginally softer tone.
PANAMAX
A quieter end to the week in terms of reported fixture volume, especially when compared to yesterday, with sentiment remaining negative across both basins. Brokers reported that while fresh cargo volume was down today in the Atlantic, tonnage is looking tighter off the North Continent. The Aurora Borealis (82,315 2023) open Gibraltar 30 July was reported fixed via North Coast South America to Spain-Portugal with grains at $22,250 to Cargill, with brokers highlighting that the premium achieved appears to be attributed to the absence of EU ETS costs. Raffles were linked to the Beleza (75,093 2008) open Tuticorin 21 July with some suggesting she fixed on a trip basis APS East Coast South America to Singapore-Japan with grains at $18,400 plus $840,000 ballast bonus. The Pacific remains oversupplied with tonnage, with limited cargo availability, particularly from the North Pacific and Australia. Market sources stated that Owners are reducing offers in an attempt to entice Charterers into negotiations during limited activity, however with sentiment remaining soft, many market participants are now said to be waiting until next week. The P5TC dropped by a further $361 to conclude the week at $18,213.
SUPRAMAX
A typically quiet end to the week which has seen bearish sentiment and rates begin to come off. The North American routes have dropped by more than $2,000 this week, but todays drop was less severe as there was little fresh information. The Continent hasn’t seen much scrap enquiry, however today EMR was rumoured to have placed an Ultramax on subjects delivery ARAG for a trip to the East Mediterranean at $25,000, although another source felt it had been fixed on voyage basis. The Mediterranean has remained positive supported by the grains season from East Med/Black Sea and there was talk of a 58,000-dwt fixed for Egypt to Rio Haina at $16,000, although $18,000 was also mentioned, and another similar type fixed for Marmara to the Caribbean at $16,500. There was also a rumour of a 64,000-dwt fixing a trip from Canakkale to Aqaba with redelivery Port Said at a very strong $24,000, but there were no further details. In the East the market was subdued with Charterers gradually pushing rates down with insufficient demand to counter the lengthening tonnage list. There was talk of the Norse Stride (66,307 2025) Bayuquan 28-29 July going on subjects for a trip via NoPac to WC India at $23,000 with Pacific Basin, but brokers said this had failed. The 11TC ended the week down $104 to finish at $21,408.
HANDYSIZE
A rather quite finish to the week as limited fresh information both from the Atlantic and Asian basins. In both the Continent and the Mediterranean there were only minimal shifts, rates slightly higher last done. The South Atlantic market remained sluggish, with tonnage levels stable and a lack of fresh demand, causing rates to stay soft. The US Gulf region also experienced a calm outlook, with no major shifts in market dynamics. The Asian market also showed little activity today with very few updates emerging, however Charterers were still bidding slightly higher than previous levels, maintaining positive sentiment. Reflecting these regional variances, the 7TC average finished the week down $25 at $16,290.

Market Fundamentals
BHP Mitsubishi Alliance Announces Mine Halt

BHP Mitsubishi Alliance, based in Australia, has halted all its mining operations in the Queensland Bowen Basin for 24 hours following a fatal accident at the Peak Downs metallurgical coal mine on 24 July, McCloskey reports. Peak Downs saleable metallurgical coal production stood 0.5 Mt higher year-on-year at 9.7 Mt (100% basis) in the financial year ending June 2026, with total Queensland production up 1.2 Mt to 37.3 Mt in the same period, according to BHP’s latest quarterly release. In the 16 July report, BHP’s total Queensland guidance for FY26/27 was 37-41 Mt on a 100% basis, weighted to the second half.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve held firm on open with the Aug and Sep contracts paid up to highs of 33900 and 36000 respectively, with the Aug v Sep roll trading again at yesterday’s high up at -2100. During the afternoon session the curve was under significant pressure in response to a weaker TA fixture being reported, which led to 32900 and 35250 sold on the Aug and Sep respectively. Sell side interest on the Q4 began to mount, hitting a floor of 35250. The Cal27 was resilient today with a trading range of 29100-29200, despite the pressure in Q4, as well as the Cal28 with 25175 printing.

PMX
The pmx market had a quiet day to finish the week. August traded between 18,500–18,750 easing into the close at 18,550, with the majority of volume concentrated around 18,650. September traded in a 19,050–19,350 range, strengthening through the session getting paid up to 19,350. Q4 26 traded 19,050–19,250, with multiple prints at 19,200–19,250 late in the day. While some second half August stems began to emerge towards the end of the week, overall enquiry levels were insuﬃcient to provide meaningful support to the market. Activity remained well behind the southern regions, with owners continuing to face a lack of fresh opportunities. Aussie remained the strongest contributor within the Pacific basin, with coal enquiries steadily increasing as the week progressed. Fresh mid August cargoes and tender activity provided some support, although a number of early August stems were still left uncovered for much of the week, we saw vsls were being fixed at sub $14,000 BKI CJK. Despite healthier cargo flow compared to other regions, the increase in demand was not enough to materially reduce vessel availability or halt the broader decline in freight levels. The Indo market experienced a softer week overall. Early in the week prompt end month coal stems dominated activity before fresh enquiry slowed, particularly through Thursday. Demand recovered slightly into Friday with fresh early August coal business, mainly into India and Southeast Asia, but prompt tonnage in the South remained plentiful, allowing charterers to maintain the upper hand. Although vessel numbers eased later in the week, supply continued to comfortably exceed demand. Overall, while cargo volumes showed gradual improvement and tonnage began to normalise towards the end of the week, the Pacific remained oversupplied. Unless vessel counts tighten further or cargo demand accelerates more convincingly, the market is likely to remain under pressure into next week, albeit with owners expected to show increasing resistance at lower levels. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场周内分化运行，好望角型船受益于太平洋和南大西洋需求支撑强势上涨（C5跳升0.74至12.85），而巴拿马型及灵便型船则因太平洋运力过剩继续承压下行。FFA曲线显示近月合约走弱，Q3 26卡姆萨型5TC报34375，较上期下跌425。整体市场情绪偏弱，预计短期灵便型船型将继续消化过剩运力。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: BDI周涨18点至2743，结构性分化明显。好望角型船逆势走强（BCI+87至4285），主因太平洋矿商活跃及南美东海岸需求回暖；巴拿马型持续下滑（P5TC-361），太平洋市场供给压力未缓解；超灵便及灵便型船维持弱势调整。FFA曲线趋平，Cal27卡姆萨型5TC报28850，市场对中长期前景谨慎。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 好望角型积极信号：三大矿商C5航线活跃，租船费率底部确认（C3至34.68）。巴拿马型谨慎：C5TC已跌破19000心理关口，太平洋市场供给过剩压制反弹空间。超灵便型偏空：北美航线本周跌幅超2000美元，运力冗余压制费率。FFA近月走弱反映短期现货市场压力。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注好望角型C3（巴西-中国）航线套利机会，现货升至34.68，Q3 26合约报34375。巴拿马型P1A_82跨大西洋航线反趋势走强（+2800美元），可关注区域供需错配。避让超灵便型南美航线，现货市场持续走软。持续跟踪太平洋煤炭货盘回升节奏，或为灵便型船提供支撑。

route_focus.view: 巴西-中国航线强势，C3指数涨0.545至34.68，南美东海岸粮运需求提供支撑，现货市场活跃度提升，关注Q3 26合约34.375的套利窗口。
跨大西洋航线逆势走强，7月24日收20141美元，较前周20000美元上方反弹，Atlantic供给趋紧但需求温和回暖，短期或维持相对抗跌。
Skaw-Passero至里约热内卢航线报8668美元，小幅上涨11美元，南大西洋灵便型船市场整体疲软，区域供需基本平衡，费率上行空间有限。
